messages.subject: Re: model comparison, no AICc estimate
parts:
AICc is undefined when (n - Npar - 1)<=0 i.e. the number of parameters in the model exceeds the number of detected individuals minus one, and it's not surprising the small sample adjustment imposes a harsh penalty when you have just one more individual. Two of your models are identical.

On Tue, Nov 24, 2015 at 11:56 PM, Julian Schmid <ju.lis.br...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi everybody,

the comparison of the following models with AIC():

secrAS51 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS5, model = g0~1, mask = AS5.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma=17), method = "BFGS")
secrAS52 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS5, model = g0~b , mask = AS5.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma=17), method = "BFGS")
secrAS53 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS5, model = list(g0~b, sigma~b), mask = AS5.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma=17), method = "BFGS")
secrAS54 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS5, model = list(g0~b, sigma~b), mask = AS5.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma=17), method = "BFGS")
secrAS55 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS5, model = g0~b+T, mask = AS5.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma=17), method = "BFGS")

gave me this result:

> model.comp
                        model                  detectfn        npar    logLik        AIC       AICc        dAICc  AICcwt
secrAS51     D~1 g0~1 sigma~1 halfnormal    3         -32.12166 70.243  82.243     NA      NA
secrAS52     D~1 g0~b sigma~1 halfnormal    4         -30.10284 68.206  108.206   NA      NA
secrAS53     D~1 g0~b sigma~b halfnormal    5         -30.10483 70.210      NA       NA      NA
secrAS54     D~1 g0~b sigma~b halfnormal    5         -30.10483 70.210      NA       NA      NA
secrAS55 D~1 g0~b + T sigma~1 halfnormal    5       -28.91803 67.836      NA       NA      NA

Does anybody have an idea what could cause the NAs for the AICc? It also seems strange that the rankings for AIC and AICc for the first to models contradict each other (according to AIC secrAS52 explains more of the variance than secrAS51 and vice versa for AICc).

In such a case, can I rely on the AIC values to choose the best model?

Thanks!
Julian
